subject: Sprint capacity grooming: temporary pool shift + autoscale exception
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint capacity grooming: temporary pool shift + autoscale exception

Team —

Quick heads-up and an ask for the Q3 sprint: BeyondCart (pilot customer) has a scheduled canary and load sweep the week of 2027-07-19. Their end-to-end test will run a concentrated set of long-context inferences and retraining-like sweeps that look like a 3x token spike for ~48 hours. They asked if we can guarantee a temporary dedicated carveout (8 GPUs) and an autoscale burst allowance up to 32 slots for the sweep window.

Why this matters:
- The test overlaps with a couple of other scheduled pilots in the core-dev pool — if we don't isolate it, we risk noisy neighbors and latency SLO violations.
- BeyondCart is on a short trial-to-paid path; successful canary materially influences their renewal decision.

What I’m requesting from infra/ops:
1) Temporary pool shift: move 8 GPUs from core-dev -> sprint-2027-beyondcart starting 2027-07-18 22:00 UTC through 2027-07-21 22:00 UTC (48h window).
2) Autoscale exception: allow burst to 32 slots for that pool for the window; bypass standard burst gating but keep all current alerting in place.
3) Ops runbook/rollback checklist so we can validate and test the change ahead of the window.

I attached a draft runbook and our q2 utilization CSV to help scope the impact. If this needs approval from Platform SLA owner or Finance for short-term cost coverage, flag now and I’ll loop the right stakeholders.

Next steps: can infra confirm whether the pool shift + exception is feasible and list any required pre-checks? If yes, I’ll schedule a short dry-run on 7/16.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: sprint-runbook.pdf, q2-pool-utilization.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint capacity grooming: temporary pool shift + autoscale exception

Thanks for the clear ask, Jonas.

Short answer: probably doable, but need to validate two things before we approve the burst exception:
- Pool interdependencies: core-dev currently has two nightly QA sweeps (00:30 UTC) and one model sweep on 7/20 that could overlap. I need to confirm whether we can shift 8 GPUs without pushing those jobs into the daytime.
- Cost and preemption: a burst to 32 slots requires temporary quota bump with the dedicated control plane and a cost owner documented; we need explicit sign-off for chargebacks.

What I can do by EOD tomorrow (7/11):
- Run the utilization simulation (using the attached CSV) and quantify projected SLO risk for core-dev.
- Draft a minimal ops-runbook for the shift and rollback, including smoke tests for latency and token throughput.

Two asks for you:
1) Can BeyondCart slide the canary start to 03:00 UTC on 7/19 (off-peak) for a 24h window? That would reduce overlap risk.
2) Assign a cost owner for the temporary burst so we can clear the quota bump.

If both line up, I’ll approve a one-time exception window and we’ll do a dry run on 7/16 as you suggested.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Dedicated Pools | Redwood Inference

On 2027-07-10 09:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Team —
>
> Quick heads-up and an ask for the Q3 sprint: BeyondCart (pilot customer) has a scheduled canary and load sweep the week of 2027-07-19.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-11T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint capacity grooming: temporary pool shift + autoscale exception

+1 to Hannah — product is supportive but we need to protect customer-facing SLAs. A couple of product asks to include in the runbook:

- Canary model fallback: If latency or error rate crosses threshold, autopromote a lighter-weight model instance (quantized variant) for BeyondCart traffic; please make sure the routing policy can shift quickly and we have a transparent metric emitted.
- Controlled ramp: start with a 10% traffic slice for the first 2 hours, then 50%, then full. Document the exact gates and metric thresholds.

I can commit a small team to own the traffic slice gating and to coordinate with BeyondCart for the staggered rollout. We should also include a post-mortem template and a set of prompt/response checks to validate output quality after fallback.

Jonas — can you confirm BeyondCart will accept the staged rollout? If they need immediate full-load, we’ll need stronger capacity guarantees or a longer reservation.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Group Product Manager, Serving | Redwood Inference

On 2027-07-10 11:03, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Thanks for the clear ask, Jonas.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-12T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint capacity grooming: temporary pool shift + autoscale exception

Approved with conditions.

Thanks for pulling this together — I reviewed the simulation Hannah ran and the utilization delta looks manageable if we stage the run and keep the maintenance window short. I’m approving a one-time pool shift and a temporary autoscale exception under these conditions:

1) Window: 2027-07-18 22:00 UTC -> 2027-07-21 22:00 UTC (exact as requested).
2) Burst cap: max 32 slots for the sprint-2027-beyondcart pool only. Global pool caps unchanged.
3) Staged rollout required: follow Karthik's ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with explicit gates.
4) Cost owner & chargeback: Jonas — you own cost reconciliation. Please confirm cost center and provide a PO or internal charge code by 7/15 EOD.
5) Alerting & runbook: Hannah to own smoke tests and rollback steps; public incident channel must be created before the window.
6) Fallback: product must have an approved quantized model variant and routing plan before the dry-run.

I’ve attached a minimal canary-ops-checklist and updated the runbook with the approval clause. I’ll file the quota bump with the control plane immediately and assign the temporary exception tag so billing can track it.

Next steps (owner):
- Jonas: confirm BeyondCart acceptance of staged rollout + provide cost center (by 7/15).
- Karthik: sign off on fallback model variant and provide gating thresholds (by 7/15).
- Hannah: finalize runbook and schedule dry-run for 7/16 (by 7/14).
- Marissa: I’ll file the quota bump and tag the exception; will notify Platform SLA owner and Finance.

Forwarding the thread to dev_patel for record and potential automation hooks.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Infrastructure Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: canary-ops-checklist.md, sprint-runbook.pdf
